end.summary:
Practised showing that sums of consecutive odd numbers starting at 1 form square numbers.
Saanvi identified 1+3=4, 1+3+5=9, and 1+3+5+7=16.
Used dot arrangements and L-shapes to connect each new odd number with the next square.
Saanvi concluded that the first 15 odd numbers sum to 225.
They initially said an odd-number sum should be odd; this mix-up was not corrected by the last seen response.
end.parentNote: Saanvi practised connecting consecutive odd-number sums to square numbers using dot patterns and L-shapes. They correctly found several early sums and used the pattern to reach 225 for the first 15 odd numbers. They mixed up the idea that adding odd numbers always gives an odd result; this was not corrected by the end of the lesson. At home, draw squares for 1, 4, 9, and 16 dots and add the next odd-number L-shape each time.
